author: Tracy2
text:
Seller A — flag OFF ("do not provide 3rd-party rates"). - Business Trip In Vietnam
Seller B — flag ON ("provide 3rd-party rates"). - OHMY TEST PREPAY

PASSED - TC1 — Partner Dotbiz, seller does NOT provide 3rd-party -> only direct rates shown. Steps: login to the Dotbiz Platform as Seller A (flag OFF); search hotels for a destination with both direct and 3rd-party rates; open a hotel and view the room/rate list. Expected: hotel list shows only hotels where OMH has a direct contract; room/rate list shows only rates from the direct contract source, no rates labelled Hotelbeds, Agoda, EAN, Dida, Dotw, Fitruums or Rakuten.

PASSED - TC2 — Partner Dotbiz, seller DOES provide 3rd-party -> full mix shown (regression). Login as Seller B (flag ON), repeat the TC1 search. Expected: result identical to what Seller B saw before this change; both direct and 3rd-party rates appear (main regression check).

PASSED - TC3 — Admin Create Booking on B2B channel, seller does NOT provide 3rd-party -> only direct rates. On oh-admin open Create Booking, pick B2B channel and Seller A, run the hotel search and view rooms/rates. Expected: behaviour matches TC1 — only direct-contract rates shown.

PASSED - TC4 — Admin Create Booking on B2B channel, seller DOES provide 3rd-party -> full mix (regression). Create Booking, B2B channel, Seller B, same search. Expected: same mix of rates as before, no regression on existing B2B sellers.

PASSED - TC5 — B2C flow is untouched. Run a regular B2C search using the same hotel as TC1/TC3. Expected: both direct and 3rd-party rates show normally; the seller flag has no effect on B2C searches.

PASSED - TC6 — Flipping the seller flag takes effect immediately on the next search. Start with Seller B (flag ON), run B2B search (direct + 3rd-party). Change Seller B flag to OFF and save, run again. Switch back to ON and save, run again. Expected: after OFF the search no longer shows 3rd-party rates; after ON the full mix returns; toggling reflected on the very next search (no wait, no manual cache clear).

author: Justin
text:
@Harry — PR ohmyhotelco/ohmyhotel-monorepo#75 is ready for review (un-drafted).

OMH-660 — web-pc layout + auth shell with JWT cookie crossover. Built the PC layout shell (header / footer / modal slot / toast) + the auth shell sharing the legacy {hostname}_userToken JWT cookie, so a user stays logged in across the legacy<->v2 Strangler flip.

Crossover replicates the legacy storage contract exactly — key, keepOnLogin localStorage/cookie branch, JSON.stringify + URL-encode round-trip, sessionStorage-mirror fallback.
Loader-direct SSR (no custom server): the root loader reads the request cookie and serializes only isAuthenticated (never the token); getServerApiClient(request) for authed loader fetches.
Auth state via useSyncExternalStore: SSR cookie flag reconciled to the live client token — a keepOnLogin (localStorage) session shows logged-in after hydration; a session-expiry clears the token + flips the shell logged-out (legacy removeToken).
Minimal-foundation scope: the login-modal port hands off to the legacy login; the full login form + SSO + current-user display are Phase 5 (OMH-460).

Verified (Node 22): typecheck + lint + 38 unit/component tests + build + 3 E2E (incl. the auth-crossover acceptance: a legacy-shaped cookie renders the authed header). Converged over 2 rounds of dual independent review — codex SHIP + quality-reviewer 5/5 SHIP.

Stacked PRs merged. #71 (OMH-653) / #72 (OMH-659) / #73 (OMH-661) are all merged (as is the independent #74, OMH-662); #75 is rebased onto master and mergeable — ready to merge.

Deferrals (see apps/web-pc/app/lib/auth/RECONCILE.md): full login/SSO + user-name display (OMH-460), i18n wiring for the shell strings, full legacy<->v2 dual-fire parity (fm-parity gate), runtime-env client injection (OMH-665/477).

author: Justin
text:
Follow-up — parked (conditional / icebox), NOT an active task.

Source: Harry's review note on OMH-659 (2026-06-30) — move the CI actions/upload-artifact uploads (Playwright HTML report + visual-regression PNG baselines) to S3 with a short lifecycle, to control GitHub Actions storage as CI scales.

Assessment (reviewed against the current workflow + config): the storage-control goal is largely already met, so an S3 migration is not warranted yet —
Both uploads already set retention-days: 7 (the same 7-day expiry an S3 lifecycle would give).
web-pc-e2e.yml is workflow_dispatch-only today (no schedule, not on the PR gate), so artifacts are generated rarely.
Artifacts are already lean: trace: on-first-retry, screenshot: only-on-failure, video off; the HTML report is a few MB and baselines upload only on capture runs.
S3 also adds real cost — bucket + CI write role (OIDC) + lifecycle + aws s3 cp glue — and loses the native run-page artifact UX.

Cheaper levers to try first (one-liners, no infra): drop retention-days to 3; switch the report upload from if: always() to if: failure() (keep always() if we still want the report on green manual runs); keep video off.

Revisit S3 only when: (1) the weekly E2E schedule OR a Playwright job on the PR gate has landed, AND (2) Actions storage is approaching the plan quota / incurring overage, and/or (3) artifacts need to be accessible outside GitHub. Suggested layout if/when we do it (Harry's): s3://omh-ci-artifacts/{playwright-reports,visual-baselines}/web-pc/<run_id>/, 7-day lifecycle.

No subtask created — tracked here as a conditional item until a trigger fires.

author: Justin
text:
@Harry — PR #74 (draft, base master) is up: new packages/shared-telemetry — the v2 central telemetry event bus + 6 sink adapters.

Delivered:
createTelemetry(): one track() validates against the shared-types DataLayerPush contract, applies cross-cutting (enable gate, per-currency money rounding, user-id hashing seam, purchase de-dup), then fans out SSR-safe (track no-ops on the server; a throwing sink can't break the others).
6 adapters: gtm (GA4/dataLayer + the ecommerce-clear ordering), meta-pixel, criteo, dable, kakao, naver — each maps the canonical event to its own vocabulary.
7th shared package (deviation from the six) — you confirmed the home; event schema reused from shared-types tracker-events. Documented in plan section 5 + RECONCILE.md.

Verified (Node 22): typecheck + test (23/23) + lint + build green.

Deferred: marketing events -> OMH-664 (GTM inventory); track() page wiring -> Phase 1+; external script loading -> host integration; Kakao OG <meta> -> route meta export. Note: typecheck uses tsc --noEmit because the repo's tsc -b --noEmit raises TS6310 on any references-package (breaks shared-data too) -> OMH-657 follow-up.

author: Justin
text:
Review round 1 (codex + quality-reviewer) — codex FIX-FIRST (6 MAJOR), quality-reviewer FIX-FIRST (3.5/5). Both independently flagged top-level money rounding + Criteo item fidelity. Fixed (commit b45ddb7b4, PR #74):
Top-level money rounding — roundPushMoney now rounds the legacy MONEY_KEYS (price/discount/value/coupon_amount/tax/refund_amount/cancel_fee) at the top level too (payment_failure / coupon_apply / cancel_confirm), not just inside ecommerce; currency lookup case-insensitive + isFinite guard.
Purchase de-dup ordering — split has/mark; the bus marks a transaction_id only AFTER a dispatch attempt, so a pre-dispatch failure can't poison the id and drop the retry.
Isolation — each sink init() is wrapped, and the transform/dispatch body is wrapped, so a throwing init or a throwing host hashUserId never reaches the calling page.
Adapter fidelity vs legacy — Criteo cart/basket/transaction send {id,price,quantity} item objects; Naver purchase uses wcs.cnv("1", amount) -> wcs_do(_nasa) (not wcs.trans); Meta purchase includes contents/content_type/content_name.
Tests +5 -> 28 total. Verified (Node 22): typecheck + test (28/28) + lint + build green.
Deferred: nested custom-dim passthrough (root cause in shared-types DataLayerEcommerceSchema/DataLayerItemSchema) -> OMH-654. Kept intentional: free-string event union, Meta device_type via config, single enabled gate (documented in RECONCILE.md).
Round 2 (verify fixes + remaining) running now.

author: Justin
text:
Review round 2 — quality-reviewer 4.5/5 SHIP-READY (one actionable: Naver inflow); codex FIX-FIRST (rated the per-sink completeness gaps MAJOR vs QR's info). Converged both to faithful legacy coverage (commit 1b330e559, PR #74):
round-money — ecommerce + items fall back to the top-level currency when ecommerce.currency is absent (legacy ecCurrency = ecommerce.currency ?? topCurrency).
Naver — purchase now fires inflow before wcs_do; added the JOIN (sign_up) + CART (add_to_cart/begin_checkout) conversions via wcs.cnv (LOG_EVENT 2/3).
Meta — Search adds search_string, CompleteRegistration adds user_id (hashed), InitiateCheckout adds num_items.
Criteo — page_view -> viewPage, page_view_main -> viewHome.
Tests +7 -> 35 total, incl. the two bus failure paths (no transaction_id poison on a pre-dispatch throw; throwing init() isolation). Verified (Node 22): typecheck + test (35/35) + lint + build green.
Round 3 (verify) running. Reviewed + left as-is: Kakao total_quantity / Criteo viewList category (non-conversion enrichment; SDKs accept the form).

author: Justin
text:
Review round 3 — quality-reviewer 4.5/5 SHIP-READY, one defect (Naver CART); codex FIX-FIRST. QR's deeper analysis corrected my round-2 Naver mapping. Fixed (commit 04bc46c98, PR #74):
Naver CART corrected — legacy fired CART(3) on the wishlist action only, value 1 (_sendWishLogToNaver) — not on add_to_cart/begin_checkout, and not the booking amount. Now add_to_wishlist -> CART(3, value 1); no Naver conversion on add_to_cart/begin_checkout.
Meta num_items dropped — round-2 sum-derivation != legacy (top-level rooms); removed (enrichment; the call site sets it precisely when the funnel page migrates).
Criteo search -> viewList(item, keywords) (legacy keyword search), not viewSearch.
Tests -> 36. Verified (Node 22): typecheck + test (36/36) + lint + build green. Deferred to dual-fire parity (documented): Criteo dates-viewSearch + viewList category; Kakao total_quantity. Round 4 (verify) running.

author: Justin
text:

Dable — added add_to_wishlist -> 'Lead' (legacy dableService.lead() on a wishlist add).

Full legacy sink-event enumeration confirms the adapters now cover the complete set: Dable 7, Meta 8, Kakao 7, Criteo full + keyword viewList; Naver JOIN/CART/PURCHASE (RESERVATION/ETC are declared but have zero legacy call sites). Deferred (additive call-site payload): Meta content_category.

author: Harry
text:
Hi @Justin Just a heads-up for later, not a request for this PR — the two actions/upload-artifact steps work fine today. But as the harness scales (weekly schedule, more pages, maybe a Playwright job on the PR gate someday), the GitHub Actions storage quota will start filling up and we'll hit overage cost ($0.25/GB-month).
When it makes sense to revisit, we could move both uploads to S3 with a lifecycle rule:
s3://omh-ci-artifacts/playwright-reports/web-pc/<run_id>/ — HTML report, auto-expire 7 days
s3://omh-ci-artifacts/visual-baselines/web-pc/<run_id>/ — captured PNGs, auto-expire 7 days
(The bucket name and paths above are just my suggestion for reference — feel free to use whatever fits your team's naming convention.)
Not urgent at all — totally fine to ship this PR as-is and revisit the S3 move whenever we add the weekly schedule or wire Playwright into the PR gate. Just parking the idea here so it's not lost.
One small thing before I approve: the PR seems to have conflicts with the base branch right now
